cases.sentence: Эта глупая ___ все еще не выводится, – сказал Вронский.
cases.explain: «старая мода» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “What’s to be done? It’s a foolish old fashion that’s kept up still,” said Vronsky.

cases.explain: «счастливые браки» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “So much the worse for those who keep up the fashion. The only happy marriages I know are marriages of prudence.”

cases.sentence: Оглянув жену и Вронского, он подошел к хозяйке и, усевшись за чашкой чая, стал говорить своим неторопливым, всегда слышным голосом, в своем обычном ___, подтрунивая над кем-то.
cases.explain: «шуточном тоне» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Glancing at his wife and Vronsky, he went up to the lady of the house, and sitting down for a cup of tea, began talking in his deliberate, always audible voice, in his habitual tone of banter, ridiculing someone.

cases.sentence: – Ваш Рамбулье в ___, – сказал он, оглядывая все общество, – грации и музы.
cases.explain: «полном составе» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Your Rambouillet is in full conclave,” he said, looking round at all the party; “the graces and the muses.”

cases.sentence: Но княгиня Бетси терпеть не могла этого тона его, sneering, как она называла это, и, как ___, тотчас же навела его на серьезный разговор об общей воинской повинности.
cases.explain: «умная хозяйка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: But Princess Betsy could not endure that tone of his—“sneering,” as she called it, using the English word, and like a skillful hostess she at once brought him into a serious conversation on the subject of universal conscription. Alexey Alexandrovitch was immediately interested in the subject, and began seriously defending the new imperial decree against Princess Betsy, who had attacked it.

cases.sentence: Алексей Александрович тотчас же увлекся разговором и стал защищать уже серьезно ___ пред княгиней Бетси, которая нападала на него.
cases.explain: «новый указ» — after the preposition «пред», the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: But Princess Betsy could not endure that tone of his—“sneering,” as she called it, using the English word, and like a skillful hostess she at once brought him into a serious conversation on the subject of universal conscription. Alexey Alexandrovitch was immediately interested in the subject, and began seriously defending the new imperial decree against Princess Betsy, who had attacked it.

cases.sentence: Вронский и Анна продолжали сидеть у ___.
cases.explain: «маленького стола» — after the preposition «у», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Vronsky and Anna still sat at the little table.

cases.sentence: Но не одни эти дамы, почти все бывшие в гостиной, даже княгиня Мягкая и сама Бетси, по нескольку раз взглядывали на удалившихся от ___, как будто это мешало им.
cases.explain: «общего кружка» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: But not only those ladies, almost everyone in the room, even the Princess Myakaya and Betsy herself, looked several times in the direction of the two who had withdrawn from the general circle, as though that were a disturbing fact. Alexey Alexandrovitch was the only person who did not once look in that direction, and was not diverted from the interesting discussion he had entered upon.

cases.sentence: Она перешла к ___ и приняла участие в общем разговоре.
cases.explain: «большому столу» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Oh, yes!” said Anna, radiant with a smile of happiness, and not understanding a word of what Betsy had said. She crossed over to the big table and took part in the general conversation.

cases.sentence: Старый, толстый татарин, кучер Карениной, в ___, с трудом удерживал прозябшего левого серого, взвивавшегося у подъезда.
cases.explain: «глянцевом кожане» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The fat old Tatar, Madame Karenina’s coachman, was with difficulty holding one of her pair of grays, chilled with the cold and rearing at the entrance. A footman stood opening the carriage door. The hall-porter stood holding open the great door of the house. Anna Arkadyevna, with her quick little hand, was unfastening the lace of her sleeve, caught in the hook of her fur cloak, and with bent head listening to the words Vronsky murmured as he escorted her down.
